answers.answer: Select number of players + 1 Factory cards face-down, return the rest unseen; place one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories; randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'number of players + 1'; '11 marked territories'; 'Randomly choose one structure bonus tile'; 'lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.'

answers.answer: Place each character at its home base; two workers, one on each of the two land-adjoined adjoining territories; four mechs over the faction abilities; six stars by the faction emblem; six technology cubes in the marked green boxes; four structures in matching Player Mat boxes; four recruits in bottom-row circles; six remaining workers on Produce red rectangles; and the action token ready beside the Player Mat. The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw. The Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objectives.
answers.evidence: Setup piece table and steps 3–4.

answers.answer: You must move the token to a different section, but may take neither action, either action, or both. Rusviet may repeat the prior section; otherwise the section must differ from last turn. If taking both, take top before bottom. Top-row gains may pay a bottom-row cost. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full first, then choose any amount of the exposed green-box benefit; costs/benefits are determined by your mat and upgrades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'may take either, both, or neither'; 'bottom first is not allowed'; 'first pay the full cost'; 'top-row gains to pay the bottom-row cost.'

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except the Mill cannot produce while uncontrolled. You may pay with resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: enemy worker controls territory; 'You keep those abilities'; costs use resources from any controlled territories.

answers.answer: No: normal Move selects up to two different units, each moving one adjacent territory, so one unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A transported worker may later move itself, or may move onto a mech and be carried by its subsequent move. All units can carry any number of resources; only mechs can carry your workers, and no unit can carry your character.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: 'two different units'; carried worker may subsequently move; 'Only mechs may also carry ... your workers, never your character.'

answers.answer: The Speed-enabled mech entering enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources. You lose one popularity per worker, down to zero; having zero/insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. This is not combat. The mech's own workers cannot independently enter territory controlled by enemy workers.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy workers immediately retreat; lose one popularity per worker; workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory. Stops override Speed.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, resolve combats before the bottom-row action; the attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: 'Finish moving the other units, then resolve all combats ... attacker chooses multiple-combat order'; worker movement restriction.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card before upgrades; if the draw deck is empty, shuffle discards to form a deck, and if both are empty draw none. Built Monument adds one popularity. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity before upgrades; built Armory adds one power. Traded resources go on a controlled territory containing at least one worker. If all your workers are home, you cannot Trade for resources.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade action descriptions.

answers.answer: Pay all exposed Produce costs (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories before upgrades; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token on that territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and go in the producing village. You may decline some or all production. Newly exposed costs affect future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps 1–3: payment before choosing territories; workers from Player Mat left to right; may decline; new costs affect future actions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box to improve a top benefit and reduce a bottom cost. Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; place any mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake. Its ability applies from then on to your character and every mech, not workers. Costs vary by mat/upgrades. Even after completing all possible bottom-action pieces, you may still pay for that bottom action to gain its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: Upgrade, Deploy, and paragraph allowing payment after completing all pieces.

answers.answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; only one structure total per territory, including opponents'; Factory is allowed, lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. A Mill's bonus production territory works only while you control it; an enemy occupant can remove your control, so the Mill cannot produce then. A Mine is your personal tunnel for all your unit movement, even when an enemy controls its territory; opponents cannot use its ability.
answers.evidence: Build: placement and immovability; Mill only while controlled; Mine personal tunnel even when enemy-controlled.

answers.answer: Take a recruit from any bottom-row Player Mat section and permanently put it on any open one-time bonus space on your Faction Mat. Immediately gain the chosen space's two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is determined by the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed: Upgrade gives one power, Deploy one coin, Build one popularity, Enlist one combat card. Resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends play. In two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits sections.

answers.answer: Both combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from zero to the smaller of seven and their current power, and may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech; Rusviet People's Army adds one additional card total if workers are present. If both sides have combat mech abilities, attacker resolves theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously, add dial and card values, then each pays selected dial power from the Power Track and discards played cards face-up; card values do not cost track power. Attacker wins ties.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–4.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory/resources and places a combat star if eligible. All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy permits eligible retreating units/carried workers to adjacent lakes instead. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake; a winning defender loses none. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed at least one power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 5–6.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; discard the token and draw the card. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and token stays. Gains go to the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no additional normal action cost or mat benefit applies, including no ongoing recruit bonus.
answers.evidence: Encounters section: after Move and combats; token remains on lost entry; gains to encounter territory; no normal action costs or mat bonuses.

answers.answer: Each player's character, on its first finish of a Move action at the Factory (after winning any combat), looks at available Factory cards, chooses one, and returns the rest. Every player may take one; later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section, optional top then bottom, with usual no-repeat rule and Rusviet exception. Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or recruit bonuses. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, or three for a character/mech with Speed, subject to ordinary movement restrictions and Mine access.
answers.evidence: Factory section.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective; you must meet all requirements at the moment of reveal, though you may wait. Place its star and put both objective cards on the bottom of the deck. Normally you can score only one objective star; Saxony keeps the second card after the first and may score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section.

answers.answer: Stars are earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except two combat stars and Saxony's exception. A placed star is permanent even if power/popularity later falls, and other players' stars do not block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play, with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end section.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, collect its primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit before placing that star. If a neighbor's recruit bonus would earn a star, finish the active action, then check active player, left neighbor and right neighbor in order; stop at the sixth star. If units are intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that movement and return initiating units to where they came from; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Sixth star immediate-end sequencing paragraph.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, each star scores $4: five stars = $20. Four normal territories plus the Factory count as seven territory units (4 + 3), at $3 each = $21. Thirteen controlled resources make six complete pairs, at $2 each = $12. These categories add $53 to held coins, plus the selected structure bonus; structures qualify for that bonus even if enemies control their territories. Tiebreakers: workers + mechs + structures (not character), power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, then stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune popularity table; Factory counts as three; complete resource pairs; structures bonus eligibility; tie-break order.

answers.answer: A home base is not a territory for any game effect. Normally you cannot move back into any home base; setup and forced retreats are exceptions, as is Crimea's unlocked Wayfare. Two bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases paragraph.

answers.answer: Mountains produce metal, tundra oil, farms food, forests wood, and villages workers; lakes and the Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce terrain table; resources paragraph.

answers.answer: Any unit may pick up, carry and drop any number of resources, including mid-movement; mechs may also carry any number of your workers, but never your character. Speed adds one territory of movement to each selected character/mech, not workers. A tunnel jump costs one step, with the extra step usable before or after it; a mech may pick up/drop resources and workers mid-move. Stops for enemy units and character encounters override Speed.
answers.evidence: Move section: all units carry resources; Speed paragraph; mid-movement pickup/drop and stop rules.

answers.answer: Yes. Any unit may enter a territory held only by an enemy structure and take control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
answers.evidence: Move: enemy-structure-only territory; printed tunnels adjacent for any unit.

answers.answer: You cannot pay only part of a cost. If unable to afford any action, move the token to a different section and take neither action (a dead turn). Since Move was last used, choose a different section.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: never pay only part; inability means move token to a different section and take neither.

answers.answer: A built Armory grants one power when you take Trade; a built Monument grants one popularity when you take Bolster. These bonuses are part of those top actions. You retain the structure abilities even without control of their territory, so an enemy occupant does not take them away.
answers.evidence: Bolster, Trade and Control sections.

answers.answer: Riverwalk applies to character/mechs: Rusviet to farms and villages; Crimea to farms and tundra; Nordic to forests and mountains; Polania to villages and mountains; Saxony to forests and mountains. Nordic Swim is a separate starting ability: workers alone may cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not help character/mechs and grants no lake movement.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities table.

answers.answer: Saxony Underpass makes controlled mountains and all tunnels, including its Mine, adjacent for character/mech Move actions. Rusviet Township makes controlled villages and the Factory adjacent for character/mech Move actions. These shortcuts apply to character/mechs, not workers.
answers.evidence: Other unlocked mech abilities: Underpass and Township.

answers.answer: Saxony Disarm applies before combat on a tunnel or its Mine: the opponent loses two power on the track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery instead lets Nordic pay one power before combat to reduce the opponent's power by two, also once per combat, not per unit.
answers.evidence: Disarm and Artillery descriptions.

answers.answer: Two mechs and three workers with Rusviet People's Army may play three combat cards total (one additional card beyond the two mech cards). Workers alone never fight; the ability still requires a character/mech in combat.
answers.evidence: People's Army: two mechs and three workers allow three cards; workers alone never fight.

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare allows its character/mechs to move from a territory or home base to its own or any inactive faction home base, regardless of distance, including inactive expansion bases. It cannot enter an active opponent's home base.
answers.evidence: Crimea Wayfare description.

answers.answer: Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into its hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion lets Crimea spend one combat card once per turn as any one resource, regardless of that card's value.
answers.evidence: Crimea Scout and Coercion descriptions.

answers.answer: Nordic Seaworthy lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and retreat to an adjacent lake instead of home. Polania Submerge lets character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake; Polania does not get Nordic's adjacent-lake retreat exception. With either ability, a worker on a lake needs a mech to move off, and carried workers/resources cannot be left behind when their carrier leaves the lake.
answers.evidence: Seaworthy/Submerge lake rules paragraph.

answers.answer: Polania Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after Polania wins combat as aggressor on its turn. It does not cover popularity loss for driving off undefended workers without combat.
answers.evidence: Camaraderie description.

answers.answer: Polania may choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order. The first gain may pay the second option's cost; the printed cost must be paid, and benefits may be taken partially or not at all.
answers.evidence: Polania Meander table and encounter option rules.

answers.answer: No. A character entering an encounter territory stops and cannot move again that turn, including during Factory Move. The encounter resolves only after the whole Move action and all combats, if the character remains there.
answers.evidence: Move encounter rule; Factory says normal movement/stop restrictions apply; Encounters timing.

answers.answer: Combat-card hand count is public, but during combat you may conceal until reveal whether you committed any cards; card contents are secret until revealed. Objective contents are secret until you reveal a completed objective. Coins are not hidden, but you need not reveal their exact total when asked.
answers.evidence: Public and hidden information table.

answers.answer: Agreements are informal and unenforceable; coins are the only tangible items exchangeable (and tournament play forbids even coin exchanges for deals/alliances). A payment cannot cancel combat initiated by moving units onto opposing units: combat happens after Move, though bribes may influence its outcome.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements section.

answers.answer: Popularity 0–6: $3 per star, $2 per territory count, $1 per complete pair of controlled resources. Popularity 7–12: $4, $3 and $2 respectively. Popularity 13–18: $5, $4 and $3 respectively. Controlled lakes count; home bases do not. Resource income counts complete pairs only, so an odd leftover resource scores nothing.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and scoring notes.

answers.answer: For each adjacency tile, count each unique qualifying feature once across all your structures; rivers do not break adjacency. Adjacent tunnels are unique printed tunnels, not Mines; adjacent encounters are unique printed encounter locations even if token removed; adjacent lakes are unique lakes. Payout for each tile: 1 feature $2; 2–3 $4; 4–5 $6; 6 $9 for tunnels, and 6–7 $9 for lakes/encounters. Zero scores zero.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table and notes.

answers.answer: Structures on tunnels count structures on printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1 earns $2, 2 earns $4, 3–4 earn $6. Structures in a row count only your longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9. Structures on farms/tundras count qualifying structures combined: 1 $2, 2 $4, 3 $6, 4 $9.
answers.evidence: Structure bonus eligibility table.

answers.answer: Yes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by a defeated mech on a lake.
answers.evidence: Combat step 6.

answers.answer: No. A placed popularity star is permanent if popularity later drops, but current popularity determines final scoring. Other players' stars never block a goal, so two factions may each earn a star for the same achievement.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end: permanent star; current popularity for scoring; other players' stars do not block goals.

answers.answer: Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions in board order: Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania clockwise, omitting inactive factions. Relative seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses can be triggered by the immediate left and right neighbors; resolve active player first, then left, then right.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2–3; Ongoing recruits section.

answers.answer: A river is a border between two land territories; a lake occupies an entire hex and extends to every adjacent shoreline. A unit with an applicable lake-movement ability can enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
answers.evidence: Move river/lake paragraph.

answers.answer: No. Show the encounter card to all players when drawn, show its artwork, and read the capitalized thematic text aloud. You need not read every option aloud.
answers.evidence: Encounters: show card, artwork and read capitalized thematic text; options need not all be read.

answers.answer: There is no limit to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
answers.evidence: Control, resources and home bases: 'No limit applies to friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.'

answers.answer: Once the current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, the next clockwise player may begin their turn while the current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure timing paragraph.

answers.answer: No. The chosen top and bottom actions are each limited to once within the turn, including for Rusviet; repeating a section only waives the previous-turn section restriction.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: actions 'each limited to once within the turn, including for Rusviet.'

answers.answer: You may gain $1 instead of moving units.
answers.evidence: Move OR coins: alternatively gain $1.

answers.answer: No. Workers never return to the Player Mat; even workers that retreat to the home base stay off the mat and cannot cover a Produce cost again.
answers.evidence: Produce: 'Workers never return to the Player Mat'; retreat rules send them to home base.

answers.answer: Yes. You may attack with zero power and zero popularity, including both at zero.
answers.evidence: Combat: 'You may attack with zero power/popularity.'

answers.answer: Yes. You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit; the ordinary limit is two combat stars, except Saxony's unrestricted rule within its six available stars.
answers.evidence: Combat step 5: 'You may still fight after reaching your combat-star limit.'

answers.answer: A faction without Meander must choose one affordable option and cannot decline to choose. Unaffordable coin/popularity options cannot be selected. It may take as little of the chosen option's benefit as desired, including none.
answers.evidence: Encounters option rules.

answers.answer: No. Both combatants choose dial power simultaneously and secretly; they also secretly commit cards. Dials and card values are revealed simultaneously after both selections.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3.

answers.answer: Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: 'Announce the action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.'

answers.answer: No. Place a star as soon as you achieve a star goal; a sixth star immediately ends play. A completed objective is different: you may wait to reveal it, but must meet all requirements at the moment you reveal it, and only reveal on your own turn before or after an action.
answers.evidence: Stars: place as soon as achieved; Objectives: 'You may wait' to reveal, requirements must hold at reveal.

answers.answer: Normally, no unit may cross rivers or enter lakes. Faction and mech abilities provide exceptions.
answers.evidence: Move: units cannot normally cross rivers or enter lakes.

answers.answer: No. The recruit is permanently placed on the selected open one-time bonus space and cannot later move.
answers.evidence: Enlist: 'It cannot later move.'

answers.answer: No. Only a character triggers an encounter; merely entering with a mech or worker does not resolve or remove the token.
answers.evidence: Encounters: 'Only a character triggers an encounter.'

answers.answer: A controlled Mill adds one bonus producing territory to the normal allowance: normally up to two becomes up to three; an upgraded allowance of three becomes up to four. The Mill itself counts as one producing worker and can produce the terrain's matching token even with no actual worker present; each actual worker there also produces normally, so Mill output is added to their output. It works only while you control it.
answers.evidence: Produce Mill paragraph.

answers.answer: You control a territory if you have a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone are not stated as establishing control; without a unit or qualifying structure, you do not retain control after your last unit leaves.
answers.evidence: Control definition: unit there, or structure with no enemy unit.

answers.answer: Build costs wood; Enlist costs food.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions: 'Upgrade — oil'; 'Deploy — metal'; 'Build — wood'; 'Enlist — food.'
